If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in late horizon (day 25–30) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in mid horizon (day 15–24) to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment swings sharply (±0.33) in the last 3 days, apply a 0.5–1.0% asymmetric correction: reduce if price is rising, increase if falling.  
If forecast deviates >3% from true value in early horizon (day 1–10), apply a 1.0–2.0% correction toward historical mean if sentiment is neutral.  
If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and forecast is trending upward, cap late horizon increase at 1.0% to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and forecast is trending downward, apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias in late horizon to avoid premature bottoming.
